question: Will this polity break (end without a handoff to a successor) within 50 years?
unit: polity-years sampled every 10 years; 682 polities with peak area >= 50000 km2 and life >= 50 years
caveats: Territory is only one signal. Turchin's structural-demographic variables (population pressure, elite overproduction, state finances) are not yet in open data the lab can reach.
Cliopatria polygons are sampled at uneven time steps, so small changes can be missed.

A handoff (renaming, reform, or a revolution that kept the territory) is detected by a heuristic: a successor starting within 2 years, within 800 km, with 60% to 170% of the area. So Russia 1917 and Qing 1912 count as handoffs, not breaks.
Many short-lived polities are absent, so base rates are for the big, well-recorded states.

sources.cite: Seshat Global History Databank, Cliopatria v0.2.1 (Bennett et al. 2025, Scientific Data 12:247), CC BY 4.0
